titles.title: Quake1
titles.engine: id Quake: GLQUAKE.EXE (id gl_vidnt.c build, md5 bcf4049319feb518b8c915ac1cc8219b, 'Exe: 15:17:32 Nov 7 1997'; the compat record calls it GLQuake 1.09 / GL 0.97; VOODOO\GLQUAKE.EXE is the same file) on 1.08 data. WINQUAKE.EXE (software, 'Exe: 09:30:49 Mar 21 1997') is a second shortcut.
titles.launch_sets: The staged launcher gives 800x600x32 fullscreen on all four 1080p LCDs. PER-TITLE-STATUS says 'capped 1280x960', and that is wrong. Play Quake.bat runs `call FLEETRES.BAT -cap 1280 960` and then `GLQUAKE.EXE -width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43% -bpp 32`. The -cap branch in fleetres.c (lines 787-799) keeps the panel's aspect. It shrinks the 1920x1080 target to the largest 16:9 mode that fits under 1280x960, which is 1280x720 (all four drivers offer it). The classic 4:3 ladder under 1280x720 then stops at 800x600, because 1024x768 is taller than 720. Running an emulation of fleetres.c over the GAMERES mode lists captured 23:55-23:57 gives FR_W43/H43 = 800x600 on .123, .145, .195 and .240. The compat DB agrees: 800x600 was measured on .123 and .240 (perbox 2026-08-31, verified) and on .246 (now .195: manual record, DISPLAYCFG 800x600x32 plus an in-game frame). That record blamed the engine ('its own mode table has no 1280x960'); the real cause is the cap logic. The launcher is present and byte-identical to the library on all four LCD boxes. There is no GAMERES rule, by design (command-line title). The Software shortcut passes no mode.
titles.menu_source: GLQuake's Options > Video Options is a READ-ONLY list. It prints 'Fullscreen Modes (WIDTHxHEIGHTxBPP)' and then 'Video modes must be set from the / command line with -width <width> / and -bpp <bits-per-pixel>' (strings in GLQUAKE.EXE); nothing in it can be selected. The launcher comment and PER-TITLE-STATUS call its source 'a fixed 4:3 table'. That is also wrong: the modes are enumerated from the driver in VID_InitFullDIB. It takes EnumDisplaySettings entries with bpp>=15 and w/h<=10000, one slot per WxHxBPP. The loop stops when nummodes reaches 30 (cmp eax,0x1e at 0x415881). Slot 0 is the windowed mode, which leaves 29 fullscreen WxHxBPP entries. With 15-24 driver resolutions at 16 and 32 bpp each, 1920x1080x32 falls past slot 29. That is the measured 'Specified video mode not available' on .145. A 1920x1080x16 entry may still show up as text on some boxes, but it can never be selected. WINQUAKE.EXE does have a selectable menu, but it only lists 8-bpp DIB modes with w<=1280 and h<=1024 (cmp 0x500/0x400 at 0x40c83d), so 1920x1080 can never appear there.
titles.evidence: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Quake1/Play Quake.bat; provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c 787-821; scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py NEW_GLQUAKE + new_launcher call_cap(1280,960); .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/fleetres_cap_emulation.py and .out.txt; .../disasm/glquake_modelist_cap30.txt (the 30-slot cap at 0x415881; the -current path at 0x415e3d writes GetSystemMetrics into modelist[1] and sets leavecurrentmode [0x8094a0]; VID_SetFullDIBMode at 0x414470 skips ChangeDisplaySettingsA when that flag is set; -force at 0x415f49 only adds a mode while nummodes<30); .../disasm/winquake_dib_1280x1024.txt; .../compat_render_measured.txt; .../deployed/{123,145,195,240}-Quake1-Play_Quake.bat (== staged md5 b263c4414c); strings '-current','-force','-conwidth','-conheight','vid_describemodes' in GLQUAKE.EXE.
titles.fix: Launch change, using a switch the stock binary already has: `GLQUAKE.EXE -current -conwidth 960 -conheight 540 +fov %FR_FOV%`. -current reads GetSystemMetrics into mode 1 and sets leavecurrentmode, so no ChangeDisplaySettings call is made and GLQuake opens a WS_POPUP at the desktop size. That bypasses the 30-slot list completely. Guard it in the launcher: use -current only when %FR_LIVE_W%x%FR_LIVE_H% equals %FR_W%x%FR_H%, i.e. the live desktop is at panel native (CLAUDE.md: never trust the live mode on its own). Otherwise fall back to `-width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43%` with the -cap removed; the cap is what produces 800x600 today. -conwidth/-conheight at 16:9 are needed because GLQuake takes its projection aspect from the 640x480 virtual console (id GPL gl_rmain.c R_SetupGL; not measured on the boxes). The in-game menu cannot be fixed with the stock GLQuake or WinQuake binaries: the GL menu cannot select a mode at all, and the software menu stops at 1280x1024. Only a source port would give an in-game 1920x1080 option (e.g. QuakeSpasm, which does in-game resolution changes and accepts protocol 15, per the web). No such port is on the share: a case-insensitive search of Files/, Utility/, DiskImages/ and transmission/ for quakespasm, ezquake, darkplaces, fitzquake, mark v, vkquake, proquake, joequake, fte, tyrquake, ironwail and *quake* found only id's own zips and Quake3e. Multiplayer: none of these switches changes the wire protocol, so the fleet NetQuake server (192.168.1.132:26000) is unaffected.
titles.fix_source: The switches are already in GLQUAKE.EXE on the share ('-current' @0x450e20, '-conwidth' @0x450de0, code verified). The launcher text comes from scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py (NEW_GLQUAKE and the GLQUAKE.EXE branch of new_launcher). An in-game menu would need a port downloaded from quakespasm.sourceforge.net; whether current builds run on 32-bit XP is unverified.
titles.fix_risk: Low for -current: it is a stock switch, needs no file edits, and never changes the mode, so nothing has to be restored on exit. Remaining risks: the live desktop not being at native (the guard covers this); the read-only video menu keeps the old label on mode 1; 16:9 aspect and FOV are unmeasured. Dropping the cap alone depends on 1280x960x32 being within the 29 slots on each box. That was measured on .145 only; with -bpp 32, a miss is a hard Sys_Error. tests/python/test_fleetres_staging.py (test_only_the_measured_ceilings_carry_a_cap, test_glquake_cap_is_the_measured_ceiling_not_the_old_guess) pins the cap and has to change together with it.
titles.hw_check: 1) EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Quake1" "Play Quake.bat". While it runs, DISPLAYCFG get should read 800x600x32 today; also take WINLIST. 2) The menu is keyboard-navigable, and synthetic keys reach GLQuake in fullscreen (per the .246 record): Esc > Options > Video Options, then F11 (bound in ID1\autoexec.cfg) to write ID1\quakeNN.tga, and DOWNLOAD it (GDI capture is black on Win7 .195). For the exact enumerated list, launch with -condebug, type `vid_describemodes` in the ~ console, then DOWNLOAD ID1\qconsole.log. 3) Proof of the fix: from C:\Games\Quake1 run GLQUAKE.EXE -current -conwidth 960 -conheight 540. DISPLAYCFG should stay at 1920x1080, WINLIST should show the GLQuake popup at 0,0-1920x1080, and the F11 TGA should be 1920x1080 with round objects not stretched. Then `connect 192.168.1.132` once. Afterwards taskkill /f /im "GLQUAKE.EXE" and delete qconsole.log and the TGAs.
titles.verifier_notes: PER-TITLE-STATUS row, launcher comment and the .246 compat note all misstate the mechanism (fixed table / 1280x960). README-FLEETRES's FLEETRES.EXE size is stale: every staged copy is 30,208 B (md5 bb180f3b...), matching provisioning/fleetres/FLEETRES.EXE. stage-fleetres.py --check reports all 213 launchers 'already current' because it only looks for the CALL marker, so it cannot see cap drift.

titles.title: Quake2Complete
titles.engine: id Tech 2: retail Quake II 3.20 (quake2.exe md5 57dd2cf4ba176f3e6ae72fccc94c38b4, 'Oct 16 1998 Win32 RELEASE'; ref_gl.dll b6d33427..., ref_soft.dll 203dc879...), with baseq2, xatrix, rogue and ctf.
titles.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8) on all four LCDs. Each of the 4 launchers calls FLEETRES with no cap, writes <mod>\fleetres.cfg (`set gl_mode "%FR_Q2MODE%"` + vid_fullscreen 1) and passes `+set gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE%`. Every mod's autoexec.cfg ends with `exec fleetres.cfg`. The GAMERES idtech2 rule (gameres.h 702-705) writes the same file at sync time. FR_Q2MODE=8 on all four, both from GAMERES target.q2mode and from the emulation. Measured 1280x960 on .123 and .240 (verified) and on .246/.195 (verified from the engine F11 TGA, 1280x960). A 2026-09-01 record from the 6-box multiplayer test shows 1024x768 on .145; how that session was launched is unknown, and today's launcher should give 1280x960 there. Present and byte-identical on all four boxes. 1280x960 is 4:3, so the panel scaler stretches or pillarboxes it.
titles.menu_source: Hardcoded in quake2.exe. vid_modes[] sits at file offset 0x543d0: 10 entries of {desc,w,h,mode}, from 'Mode 0: 320x240' through 'Mode 8: 1280x960' and 'Mode 9: 1600x1200'. The Options > Video 'video mode' spinner uses the matching label array '[320 240  ]' '[400 300  ]' '[512 384  ]' '[640 480  ]' '[800 600  ]' '[960 720  ]' '[1024 768 ]' '[1152 864 ]' '[1280 960 ]' '[1600 1200]'. ref_gl gets its size only through Vid_GetModeInfo(gl_mode). There is no custom mode and no 16:9 entry.
titles.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/quake2_320_modes_and_menu.txt and menus/idtech2_vid_modes_tables.txt (entry offsets); /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Quake2Complete/Quake II*.bat, baseq2|xatrix|rogue|ctf/autoexec.cfg (exec fleetres.cfg last), xatrix|rogue/config.cfg (staged gl_mode 6, overridden); agent/shared/gameres.h 295-300 and 702-705; fleetres_cap_emulation.out.txt; compat_render_measured.txt; deployed/*-Quake2Complete-Quake_II.bat == staged.
titles.fix: 3.20 has no config-only route. The smallest concrete change is a byte patch to Quake2Complete's quake2.exe: vid_modes[9] width at 0x54464 from 1600 to 1920 and height at 0x54468 from 1200 to 1080, plus the same-length strings 'Mode 9: 1600x1200' to 'Mode 9: 1920x1080' and '[1600 1200]' to '[1920 1080]'. FLEETRES and gameres (q2tab/gr_q2tab and the idtech2 writers) then need to pick gl_mode 9 when FR_W x FR_H is 1920x1080, and add `set fov %FR_FOV%`. id Tech 2 is vert- at 16:9 but not stretched, because V_RenderView derives fov_y from the refdef aspect. Nothing on the fleet uses mode 9 today: FLEETRES's 4:3 ladder never goes above 1280x960 here. A cleaner alternative is the Yamagi Quake II client (r_mode -1 + r_customwidth/height and a real video menu). The fleet server is already Yamagi 8.60 on protocol 34. For XP there is the akosela/yquake2-xp fork, based on 8.01 (web). No Yamagi, KMQuake2, Q2PRO or R1Q2 build is on the share (case-insensitive search).
titles.fix_source: The patch needs no download: the bytes are in the staged quake2.exe at the offsets above. Yamagi would need downloading (yamagi.org / github yquake2, or akosela/yquake2-xp). It must be a 32-bit build, because all four LCD OS installs are 32-bit.
titles.fix_risk: The patch modifies a retail exe shared by 4 launchers. 3.20 draws the HUD, console and menus at 1:1 pixels, so they are tiny at 1080p. Never point ref_soft at mode 9 (id GPL ref_soft r_local.h has MAXWIDTH 1600; source knowledge, not binary-verified). Quake2Win9x ships the identical exe, so patch only Quake2Complete's copy. Multiplayer: protocol 34 has no client-exe or pure check, so joining 192.168.1.132:27910 should be unaffected; prove it with one join. Yamagi is a new client and game-DLL stack, and all boxes should switch together.
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Quake2Complete" "Quake II.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1280x960. The menu is keyboard-navigable: Esc > Options > Video, and the arrow keys cycle 'video mode'. Press F11 to write baseq2\scrnshot\quakeNN.tga and DOWNLOAD it (GDI is black on .195). The list should end at [1600 1200]. After a patch: the list should show [1920 1080]; selecting it and applying should give DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080 and a 1920x1080 F11 TGA, and `connect 192.168.1.132:27910` should still join.
titles.verifier_notes: The staged autoexec comment says Q2 execs autoexec.cfg BEFORE VID_Init. In id's CL_Init, FS_ExecAutoexec runs after VID_Init; gl_mode then applies through the modified-cvar vid restart, and the +set on the command line sets the first mode anyway. The outcome is correct; the comment is not.

titles.title: Quake2Win9x
titles.engine: id Tech 2: the same Quake II 3.20 binaries; quake2.exe, ref_gl.dll and ref_soft.dll are md5-identical to Quake2Complete's. Base game only, with COMMAND.COM launchers.
titles.launch_sets: Nothing runs on the LCD boxes. requires.json has max_os win9x, and the published gate verdicts say 'no  Quake2Win9x  os  OS too new for this title (have winxp|win7, max win9x)' for all four LCD profiles (_gamegate e633518d4747e4f2 .123, bb7a13d03d67b0b4 .145, 7cf5bd34eefa68a7 .195, cab829af7a354f22 .240). DIRLIST C:\Games on .123, .145, .195 and .240 confirms it is absent (case-insensitive). Its launchers hardcode sw_mode 3 or gl_mode 3 (640x480, no FLEETRES) for .243's Win98 + Voodoo 2 CRT box. The gate currently refuses it there too, for disk (197 MB free < 260).
titles.menu_source: Same hardcoded Quake II 3.20 table as Quake2Complete: vid_modes 'Mode 0: 320x240'..'Mode 9: 1600x1200' and the menu labels '[320 240  ]'..'[1600 1200]'.
titles.evidence: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Quake2Win9x/requires.json (max_os win9x); the Play Quake II*.bat files (sw_mode/gl_mode 3); .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/gamegate_verdicts_lcd_boxes.txt; deployed/summary.json ('ABSENT (case-insensitive)' on all four); md5 57dd2cf4... for both quake2.exe copies.
titles.fix: None needed: the OS gate means it never deploys to a 1080p LCD. If Quake2Complete's exe is patched for 1080p, leave this tree's copy stock; it serves the 640x480 Win9x/Voodoo lane.
titles.hw_check: DIRLIST C:\Games on each LCD box: Quake2Win9x must stay absent. It was absent on all four on 2026-09-29, and GAMESYNC STATUS counts it in titles_gated. The resolution check itself belongs on .243, not on the LCD boxes.

titles.title: HexenII
titles.engine: Raven Hexen II retail (install.reg says v1.03). glh2.exe is a GLQuake-derived OpenGL build (md5 c450ea8ac9aefa9e4a5b48e9c7ae4e66, 'Exe: 15:08:09 Sep 4 1997'; VOODOO\GLH2.EXE is identical); h2.exe is the software build.
titles.launch_sets: Not 1080p, and not even the same mode on every box. Play, Host and Join Hexen II.bat run `call FLEETRES.BAT -cap 1024 768` and then `glh2.exe -width %FR_W% -height %FR_H%`, with no -bpp. The -cap branch in fleetres.c keeps 16:9. On .123 and .240 the drivers offer 848x480, so FR_W/H = 848x480. On .145 and .195 no 16:9 mode fits under the cap, so FR_W/H is the cap itself, 1024x768 (emulation on the captured mode lists). Measured: 848x480 on .123 and .240 (perbox 2026-08-31), and 1024x768 at 16 bpp on .246/.195 (DISPLAYCFG). Without -bpp, glh2 tries 15 and 16 bpp first. The launchers are present and byte-identical on all four boxes. No GAMERES rule (command-line title). PER-TITLE-STATUS says '1080p, measured on .145 1920x1080', but that predates the cap, which was added 08-31 after .240 refused 1280x960 and above. tests/python/test_lan_multiplayer_library.py asserts that the cap yields 'FR_W=1024 FR_H=768', which is false on .123 and .240.
titles.menu_source: Options > Video Modes is the same READ-ONLY GLQuake list: 'Fullscreen Modes (WIDTHxHEIGHTxBPP)' plus 'Video modes must be set from the / command line with -width <width> / and -bpp <bits-per-pixel>' (strings in glh2.exe). Its entries are the driver-enumerated modelist, capped at 30 slots (cmp ecx,0x1e at 0x4308e2; bpp>=15, w/h<=10000). That cap explains both measurements: .240 answered 'Specified video mode not available' at 1280x960, 1280x1024 and 1920x1080 because the list filled before those modes, while .145 accepted 1920x1080 at 16 bpp. What appears is box-dependent, and nothing can be selected. h2.exe (software) has a selectable menu, but only 8-bpp DIB modes with w<=1280 and h<=1024 (cmp 0x500/0x400 at 0x415e6d).
titles.evidence: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/HexenII/Play Hexen II.bat, Host Hexen II - LAN.bat, Join Hexen II - LAN.bat (-cap 1024 768); .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/disasm/hexen2_modelist_cap30.txt (the 30-slot cap; the -current path at 0x430e32 through GetSystemMetrics [0xdf76ec]; h2.exe limits); fleetres_cap_emulation.out.txt; compat_render_measured.txt (848x480 on .123/.240, 1024x768 on .246); deployed/*-HexenII-*.bat == staged; scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py TITLES['HexenII'] (no cap); tests/python/test_lan_multiplayer_library.py 44-99.
titles.fix: Launch change: replace the cap with the stock -current switch that glh2.exe carries (string @0x468a48; same GetSystemMetrics + leavecurrentmode code as GLQuake), giving `glh2.exe -current -heapsize 32768 -nocdaudio ...`. Guard it with FR_LIVE_W/H == FR_W/H, and otherwise use `-width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43%` with no cap. -current can never hit 'Specified video mode not available', so the Host launcher's listen server is safe. glh2 has no -conwidth switch, so whether the 16:9 aspect is correct is unknown. The in-game menu cannot be fixed with stock glh2 or h2. Only a source port would do it, e.g. Hammer of Thyrion (uHexen2), which has in-game resolution changing (web). It is not on the share (case-insensitive search found nothing). Whether HoT interoperates with retail glh2 listen servers is unverified, so all boxes would have to move together.
titles.fix_source: -current is already in glh2.exe on the share. The launcher recipe lives in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py TITLES['HexenII'], which today emits no cap; the -cap on the share was added outside the generator. A port would need downloading (uHexen2 1.5.x Windows build, sourceforge.net/projects/uhexen2).
titles.fix_risk: Low to medium. It is a stock switch, but it depends on the live desktop mode (hence the guard), and aspect at 16:9 is unmeasured. The LAN tests (test_hexen2_gl_launchers_cap_to_a_mode_the_engine_has and _cap_the_engine_at_1024x768) require the cap and must be rewritten with the change. Host and join then have to be re-proven on two boxes (scripts/game-servers/nqquery.py <ip> 26900 HEXENII).
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\HexenII" "Play Hexen II.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 848x480 on .123/.240 and 1024x768x16 on .145/.195 today. The menu is keyboard-navigable: Esc > Options > Video Modes. F11 writes data1\shots\hexenNN.pcx; DOWNLOAD it. Proof of the fix: glh2.exe -current -heapsize 32768 -nocdaudio. DISPLAYCFG should stay at 1920x1080, WINLIST should show class HexenII at 0,0-1920x1080, and the F11 frame should be 1920x1080; check it for stretch. Then run Host - LAN with -current on one box, confirm nqquery.py <ip> 26900 HEXENII answers, join from a second box, and screenshot both. Delete the PCX files afterwards.
titles.verifier_notes: Three sources disagree. PER-TITLE-STATUS and PER-TITLE-CHANGES say 1080p. The stage-fleetres.py recipe emits no cap. The staged launchers and the LAN test enforce -cap 1024 768. stage-fleetres --check calls them current.

titles.title: SiNGold
titles.engine: Ritual SiN (an id Tech 2 derivative), patched to the official 1.11 (sin.exe md5 8d320d7fc3ea3a226ec98dafef3e81ba, built 'Jan 22 2001'), with the Wages of SiN mission pack (2015\) and ctf\.
titles.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8). Play SiN Gold.bat and Play Wages of SiN.bat call FLEETRES, write base\ or 2015\fleetres.cfg (gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE% + vid_fullscreen) and pass +set gl_mode. Both autoexec.cfg files end with exec fleetres.cfg, and the GAMERES idtech2 rows cover base and 2015. Measured 1280x960 on .123 and .240 (verified) and on .246/.195 (runs). The launchers are byte-identical to the library on all four boxes. .145 cannot run the GL renderer at all: sin.exe dies creating an OpenGL context on the 8400GS GL 3.3 driver (launch.txt notes). Only 'Play SiN - software renderer.bat' works there, and it now asks for sw_mode %FR_Q2MODE% = 8 (1280x960 in software); the verified software run was 1024x768, so this is untested.
titles.menu_source: A menu data file: menus/main.mnu in base/pak5.sin (the 1.11 SPAK). Its VIDEO menu has `listitem con_vidmode 3 ... numitems 10` with " 320 x 240" " 400 x 300" " 512 x 384" " 640 x 480" " 800 x 600" " 960 x 720" " 1024 x 768" " 1152 x 864" " 1280 x 960" " 1600 x 1200". The compiled 'apply_vid_changes' function applies it against sin.exe's vid_modes (file offset 0x94450, Mode 0 320x240 … Mode 9 1600x1200). Wages of SiN's 2015/pak0.sin main.mnu says numitems 9, so its list stops at 1280 x 960.
titles.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/sin_main_mnu_video_mode.txt and menus/idtech2_vid_modes_tables.txt; /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/SiNGold/Play SiN Gold.bat, Play Wages of SiN.bat, Play SiN - software renderer.bat; base/autoexec.cfg lines 61-64, 106-108, 177; 2015/autoexec.cfg 73-76, 118-120, 189; gameres.h 706-707; compat_render_measured.txt; deployed/*-SiNGold-Play_SiN_Gold.bat == staged.
titles.fix: Same shape as Quake II. Patch sin.exe vid_modes[9]: width at 0x944e4 from 1600 to 1920, height at 0x944e8 from 1200 to 1080, and the string 'Mode 9: 1600x1200' to 'Mode 9: 1920x1080'. Ship override paks with a relabeled menus/main.mnu: base/pak6.sin (' 1600 x 1200' becomes ' 1920 x 1080') and 2015/pak1.sin (the same, plus numitems 9 becomes 10). A pak is needed because Quake II-lineage file systems search paks before loose files, so a loose file would be shadowed (inferred, needs testing). The FLEETRES/gameres idtech2 rule must then pick mode 9 on a 1920x1080 panel, and should also write con_vidmode and sw_mode (see notes). No SiN port or widescreen fix is on the share (case-insensitive search found only the GOG installer, setup_sin_gold_1.13b).
titles.fix_source: No download: the bytes are in the staged sin.exe, and the menus are in base/pak5.sin and 2015/pak0.sin.
titles.fix_risk: Medium. It modifies the 1.11 exe, the same file that solved the CD check, so keep the original. SiN's menus and HUD were laid out for 4:3 and are unmeasured at 16:9. Never send the software renderer (ref_soft_real.dll, .145's only path) to mode 9. Multiplayer: SiN LAN is box-to-box through ds_*.bat with no pure or anti-cheat check, so it should be unaffected; prove one join.
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\SiNGold" "Play SiN Gold.bat" (not on .145); DISPLAYCFG get should read 1280x960. Menu: main menu > Controls > Video > 'Video Mode:'. It is a Quake II-lineage menu, so keyboard navigation is expected but has not been proven on this fleet. F11 writes base\players\<name>\scrnshot\sin###.tga; DOWNLOAD it. The list should end at 1600 x 1200, or at 1280 x 960 in Wages of SiN. On .145, test the software shortcut at sw_mode 8.
titles.verifier_notes: fleetres.cfg (from the launcher and from the GAMERES idtech2 body) sets only gl_mode and vid_fullscreen, but both autoexec.cfg files set con_vidmode 6 and sw_mode 6. So the in-game Video Mode list reads ' 1024 x 768' while the game runs at 1280x960, and 'Apply Changes' very likely drops it to 1024x768. apply_vid_changes is compiled code; this is inferred, not traced.

titles.title: SoldierOfFortune
titles.engine: Raven Soldier of Fortune (id Tech 2 + GHOUL). The screen shows version 1.03 x86F (SoF.exe md5 2f4db3771d51d8b585bbea695041e40c). The last official patch, 1.07f, is not on the share.
titles.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8). Play Soldier of Fortune.bat calls FLEETRES, writes base\fleetres.cfg (gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE% + vid_fullscreen) and passes +set gl_mode; base\autoexec.cfg ends with exec fleetres.cfg; the GAMERES idtech2 row covers base. Measured 1280x960 on .123 (verified, ARC menu) and .240 (runs, window 0,0-1280,960). .246/.195 runs, resolution not recorded. The launcher is byte-identical to the library on all four boxes. Note that no level loads anywhere: every map raises the WON 'insert the SOF CD' error (requires.json, 2026-09-28), so only the menus can be verified.
titles.menu_source: An RMF text file, menus/m_video.rmf in base/pak0.pak: `<list "640x480,800x600,960x720,1024x768,1152x864,1280x960,1600x1200" match "3,4,5,6,7,8,9" atext "^MENU_VIDEO_RESOLUTION^ : " cvar menu_mode ...>`. menus/applyvid.cfg does `set gl_mode $menu_mode`. SoF.exe's vid_modes (file offset 0x1c6e08) starts with 'Mode 0/1/2: Unsupported' (320x240, 400x300, 512x384) and continues 'Mode 3: 640x480' through 'Mode 9: 1600x1200'.

titles.fix: Option (a), in-tree: patch SoF.exe vid_modes[9], width at 0x1c6e9c from 1600 to 1920 and height at 0x1c6ea0 from 1200 to 1080. Ship base/pak2.pak with an edited menus/m_video.rmf, either relabeling '1600x1200' as '1920x1080' or appending ',1920x1080' mapped to 9. Then teach the FLEETRES/gameres idtech2 selection about mode 9. Option (b) is the community's recommended route (web, sof1.megalag.org): SoF 1.07f plus the SoFplus client. SoFplus's _sp_cl_vid_mode_0.._9 cvars redefine what gl_mode 0..9 mean, and it comes with modified menus. SoFplus requires 1.07f (web), and neither is on the share.
titles.fix_source: (a) No download: the bytes are in the staged SoF.exe and the menu is in base/pak0.pak. (b) Would need downloading the SoF 1.07f patch and the SoFplus client from sof1.megalag.org. A case-insensitive search of the share found only SoF_Demo.exe and SoF2 files.
titles.fix_risk: The web reports that hex-patched widescreen modes clip the bottom of SoF's menus and force a switch back to 4:3 to click 'accept mission' between missions. Horizontal FOV stays fixed (vert-). Multiplayer is already blocked (WON error, and there is no SoF server on the host), so there is no multiplayer regression. A modified exe can upset SoF's anti-cheat, which is obsolete. Moving to 1.07f changes the version every box presents, so patch the library and move all boxes together.

Menu: the ARC globe, then the options folder, then Video > 'Resolution'. The input evidence conflicts: absolute UICLICK navigated this menu on .123, but on .240 the cursor moved by relative deltas and UIKEY reached neither the menu nor the modal. Treat it as needing a human. F11 writes a screenshot; the staged tree has user\scrnshot while the autoexec comment says base\scrnshot, so check both and DOWNLOAD it.

titles.title: Doom3
titles.engine: id Tech 4: official DOOM 3 1.3 (version.inf ExtVersion=1.3; DOOM3.exe md5 7cd77c22b38c223ef1047083e374875a, 5,832,704 B, no SafeDisc; base/gamex86.dll is game03.pk4's 2005-05-10 build). The d3xp (Resurrection of Evil) paks are present.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 on all four LCDs. Play DOOM 3.bat and Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat call FLEETRES with no cap and run `DOOM3.exe +set r_mode -1 +set r_customWidth %FR_W% +set r_customHeight %FR_H% +set r_aspectRatio %FR_D3AR% +set r_fullscreen 1`, where FR_D3AR=1 because 1920*9 == 1080*16. id Tech 4 re-applies +set after DoomConfig.cfg, so the command line wins, and no DoomConfig.cfg is staged. r_aspectRatio does not occur in DOOM3.exe, but the 1.3 game DLL registers it ('aspect ratio of view: 0 = 4:3 1 = 16:9 2 = 16:10'). That DLL loads after the command line is applied, so the value is kept. Measured: 1920x1080 verified on .123 and .240 (2026-08-31), and DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080x32 on .246/.195 (no frame, because GDI is black on Win7). .145 is untested. The launchers are present and byte-identical on all four boxes. Doom3 is still deployed on .240 even though today's gate refuses it there for disk (1490 MB < 1600).
titles.menu_source: base/pak007.pk4 guis/mainmenu.gui is the effective copy. Its System 'Screen Size' control (#str_02153) is `choiceDef OS2Primary { choices "#str_04222" values "3;4;5;6;7;8" cvar "r_mode" choiceType 1 }`. strings/english.lang maps #str_04222 to "640x480;800x600;1024x768;1152x864;1280x1024;1600x1200". d3xp/pak001.pk4's mainmenu.gui has the same choiceDef. DOOM3.exe's r_vidModes run from Mode 0 320x240 to Mode 8 1600x1200. Neither GUI has any aspect-ratio control. With the launcher's r_mode -1, the choiceDef finds no matching value and shows index 0, '640x480', while the game actually runs at 1920x1080. Touching that control and restarting video drops to r_mode 3-8 for the session; the next launch restores 1080p.
titles.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/doom3_mainmenu_screensize.txt; /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Doom3/Play DOOM 3.bat, Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat, version.inf; base/game03.pk4 gamex86.dll (r_aspectRatio string); scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py doom3_args(); scripts/game-servers/doom3/entry.sh (si_pure 0; notes that dhewm3 is not network-compatible with retail 1.3); compat_render_measured.txt; deployed/*-Doom3-Play_DOOM_3.bat == staged; gamegate_verdicts_lcd_boxes.txt.
titles.fix: Ship an override pk4 that sorts after pak007.pk4, e.g. base/zz_fleetvideo.pk4, plus d3xp/zz_fleetvideo.pk4 for RoE. It holds a copy of guis/mainmenu.gui with only the Screen Size choiceDef edited: choices '640x480;800x600;1024x768;1152x864;1280x1024;1600x1200;Native' and values '3;4;5;6;7;8;-1'. The label should be 'Native' rather than '1920x1080', because r_customWidth/Height are set per box by FLEETRES and '1920x1080' would be false on CRT boxes. Add one new choiceDef on cvar r_aspectRatio: choices '4:3;16:9;16:10', values '0;1;2'. Nothing on the share does this. dhewm3 is absent and, per the repo's own server script, not network-compatible with 1.3. D3EE (web) adds menu resolutions but is not on the share and changes the game.
titles.fix_source: No download: this edits files already in the tree (guis/mainmenu.gui from base/pak007.pk4 and d3xp/pak001.pk4) and packages them into a new pk4.
titles.fix_risk: Low to medium. A 700 KB id GUI script gets replaced by a copy, so edit only that choiceDef and diff the result against the original. The fleet doom3-server runs si_pure 0, so an extra client pk4 does not break fleet multiplayer; behaviour on pure internet servers is unverified. The HUD and menus stay 640x480-virtual and stretch at 16:9, which is cosmetic.
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Doom3" "Play DOOM 3.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1920x1080x32. The menu is driven by a mouse cursor (DirectInput, expected to be relative) and has no keyboard navigation. Checking Settings > System > Screen Size therefore needs a human, unless one UICLICK test proves otherwise. Keyboard-only check: open the console with Ctrl+Alt+~, query r_mode, r_customWidth, r_customHeight and r_aspectRatio, run listModes, then `condump fleetres_check.txt` and DOWNLOAD it (expected under C:\Games\Doom3\base). `screenshot` should write base\screenshots\shot00000.tga; an earlier attempt on .195 found nothing, so confirm the path. After the pk4 fix, the Screen Size control must read 'Native' while r_mode is -1. Delete the dump and screenshot afterwards.
titles.verifier_notes: Doom3 is missing from the 'Every title' table in PER-TITLE-STATUS.md. Resurrection of Evil has no desktop shortcut; it is reached through the in-game Mods menu, and whether the +set values survive that restart was not checked.
